verdict.rationale: Buzz ships multiple official developer-facing building blocks — a documented CLI (buzz-cli), an ACP harness (buzz-acp) that lets goose/codex/claude-code agents plug in, a provider-agnostic agent runtime (buzz-agent) that is itself an MCP client, a Persona Pack spec, and open wire protocols (NIP-29/NIP-42/NIP-AA) that third-party clients can connect to directly. This gives AI-native builders real official surfaces to target, but there is no traditional multi-language SDK library, and probes show no OpenAPI spec or llms.txt (404s), so 'SDK' support is protocol/CLI-based rather than packaged client libraries. Missing for 10: language-specific SDK packages (Python/JS/Go clients), published OpenAPI/REST SDK, and independent third-party confirmation that developers have built against these interfaces.
